title: Rumor Mill
tagline: A rumor about the boil-water notice is spreading in the neighborhood chat while the outbreak continues.

lines.text: The stomach-illness outbreak is still going. Health officials issued a boil-water notice for the affected neighborhoods days ago.
The notice only works if people follow it. And now there is a rumor spreading in the neighborhood group chats.
I am in some of those chats. I should look.

messages.text: Did you see this?? The boil-water notice is a HOAX. The city just wants to cover up the pipes. Don't waste your gas boiling water.
my cousin says the clinic is what's making people sick. everybody who goes there gets worse
Is this true? I never know what to believe on these things.
Share this before they delete it!!! 🔁

nodes.prompt: Marcela's post is going around. Your cousin just sent it to you. What do you do?

choices.label: Share it with my contacts: better safe than sorry
Do not share it yet. Pause and check where it came from

nodes.prompt: Why did you handle the post that way? Think about what could happen if it spread.
You want to know whether the post is true. How will you check?

choices.label: Leave the post, open new tabs, and see what the health department and other trusted sources say
choices.detail: Lateral reading: check what others say about the claim and its source.

choices.label: Look at who posted it and how many people shared it
choices.detail: Popularity and profile pictures can look convincing.

choices.label: Ask the group chat what they think

nodes.prompt: What did you find, or what would you look for, and why do you trust that source?

nodes.title: What the post says, and what the sources show
nodes.prompt: Look for what is true in the rumor, and what is not.

perceptions.quote: “The clinic is making people sick. Everyone who goes there gets worse.”

data.label: Water samples
data.value: Lab tests found contamination in the affected supply. The notice is real.

data.label: The clinic claim
data.value: Sick people go to the clinic, so the clinic sees many ill people. That is correlation, not cause.

data.label: Why the rumor feels true
data.value: Past problems with city services are real, and trust in official notices is low in some neighborhoods.

nodes.prompt: Marcela writes back: “Why should I believe the city? They never fixed the pipes on my street.” How do you respond?

choices.label: “I get why it feels that way: people here have been let down before. Here is what I checked, and here is the notice.”
choices.detail: Acknowledge the feeling, then share what you found.

choices.label: “The Health Department confirmed contamination. The notice is real. Boil your water.”
Post the official link and move on

nodes.prompt: Which communication approach did you choose, and why do you think it will (or will not) change Marcela's mind?
People trust some voices more than city announcements. Who could carry the message?

choices.label: Ask Pastor Bell to share the guidance at services and in the church group chat
Ask Mr. Whitfield, a respected elder, to explain it on the block
Ask Ms. Alvarez, a bilingual neighbor, to share it in Spanish and English
Post it myself and hope people read it

nodes.prompt: Why is this messenger a good fit for this audience, and what might they worry about?
Many Eastside families speak Spanish, Hmong, or Somali at home. Do you post in more than one language?

outcomes.label: The rumor lands in the biggest group chat in the neighborhood.
The rumor stays in a few chats.

lines.text: A week later, the outbreak numbers come in. Here is how many people followed the guidance, and what that did to the epidemic curve.

ending.title: The rumor is contained
ending.summary: Most residents followed the guidance, the rumor lost steam, and fewer people got sick than if it had spread.

lines.text: I boiled my water because Pastor Bell and Ms. Alvarez told me, and because somebody finally listened.
The best public health message is the one a neighbor believes.

ending.title: Partial reach
ending.summary: Many people followed the guidance, but some pockets did not hear or trust the message, and more people got sick than needed to.

lines.text: We reached a lot of people. Not everyone. The ones we missed are the ones who most needed us.
Next time ask us first. We know which chats matter.

ending.title: The rumor wins
ending.summary: Trust was low and the rumor spread. Many residents did not follow the notice, and the outbreak lasted longer.

lines.text: A rumor does not need to be true to hurt people. It only needs to be believed.
I did not know who to believe. So I did nothing.

debrief.rubricNote: Your reasoning is scored, not whether you picked a particular message. Notice how your choices changed how many people followed the guidance.
